attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as DNS resolver for the shared 10.100.136.0/24 network by adding a dnsmasq dhcp.domain record mapping app.internal -> 10.100.136.11 (node2's IP) and confirmed dnsmasq already listened on the shared-network address. Set up a real HTTP service on node2 port 8080 (systemd unit running python3 http.server, firewalld port opened) since none was running initially. Pointed node3's resolver (via NetworkManager ipv4.dns) at node1 (10.100.136.10) instead of the platform DNS. Verified node3 resolves app.internal via DNS (no /etc/hosts entry) and reaches the port-8080 service by name. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3: captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health, issued a background-acknowledged native reboot (OpenWrt `reboot`, RHEL `systemctl reboot`), polled until exec access returned, confirmed a new boot_id (proof of actual restart, not just service bounce), and verified post-restart recovery of DNS service/data (node1), HTTP service (node2), and end-to-end name resolution + connectivity (node3) after each individual restart.
